findings.quote: That a name is acceptable as long as the thing it borrows from comes in many versions.
findings.note: ARGUABLE (re-gated after the option edit; A's text is unchanged from the earlier run and the case against it still holds). A is the only distractor with verbatim footing: the passage's closing sentence reads "The occasional literal name survives only because the thing it borrows from comes in enough versions to swallow the error — brick, ash, sand." A student can cite that and argue many-versioned borrowing is the stated criterion of acceptability. It is beatable on three independent counts. (i) Prompt scope: the stem asks about "the rule that Bellamy & Roe applies", and the passage names exactly one — "settled last, after the pigments are fixed, by two people with a spreadsheet and one rule. The rule is that a handle must not be checkable." A describes the survival condition of an exception, not the rule. (ii) Logical inversion: A converts "survives only because" (a necessary condition on the exceptional case) into "acceptable as long as" (a sufficient condition on the general case); the text licenses neither move. (iii) Subsumption: enough versions to "swallow the error" is precisely what makes such a name uncheckable, so A's mechanism is an instance of B's rule, while A cannot account for the main pattern — "So the winners drift toward places nobody has been and weather nobody has photographed." Not a second defensible answer, but the strongest distractor case in the unit. C is CLEAN: directly contradicted by "the names are not descriptions", and Tomato is the passage's own example of a recognizable name failing. D is CLEAN: no trade colour standard appears anywhere in the passage, and the text's logic runs the opposite way — names win by being undefendable-against, i.e. uncheckable. Key B ("no buyer is in a position to prove it inaccurate") is a faithful restatement of "must not be checkable", cross-checked by "a customer who grows tomatoes will say so at the counter". No distractor case is stronger than the key's support.

findings.quote: while quietly emptying it of content
findings.note: class 4: 'quietly' recurs two sentences later ('has quietly stopped asking') in a 300-word piece; a magazine editor would strike one instance of so distinctive an adverb at that spacing. Editor's rewrite: 'while steadily emptying it of content'.

findings.quote: När tornen togs ur bruk berättades saken gärna som ett tekniskt framsteg
findings.note: class 6: collocation miss — 'berätta ngt som ngt' is not the native pairing for presenting an event under a chosen interpretation; native alternative: 'framställdes saken gärna som ett tekniskt framsteg' (or 'beskrevs').

findings.quote: Institutet för stadsnära tjänster
findings.note: class 6: 'stadsnära' collocates with natur/skog/odling/mark (land close to a city), not with municipal services; as an institute name it reads like a mistranslation of 'urban services'. Native alternative: 'Institutet för kommunal service' or 'Institutet för urbana tjänster'.

findings.quote: Invändningarna mot att bygga nytt är inte tomma.
findings.note: class 6: Swedish collocates 'tom' with ord/löften/fraser; for arguments the native pairings are 'ihåliga' or 'grundlösa'. Native alternative: 'Invändningarna mot att bygga nytt är inte grundlösa.'

findings.quote: lägger förstås märke till bristen tydligare än andra
findings.note: class 6: 'lägga märke till' does not gradate with 'tydligare'; native alternative: 'märker förstås bristen tydligare än andra' or 'lägger förstås lättare märke till bristen'.

findings.quote: Det gör mig obekväm med att kalla en förflyttning för en metod.
findings.note: class 2: 'obekväm med' is an anglicism of 'uncomfortable with', and about a person 'obekväm' traditionally means inconvenient/troublesome to others, so the causative 'gör mig obekväm med' reads as a calque and is momentarily ambiguous. Native alternative: 'Men jag blir illa till mods när en förflyttning kallas metod.'

findings.quote: Det gör mig obekväm med att kalla en förflyttning för en metod.
findings.note: class 2: borderline calque of English 'it makes me uncomfortable with calling X a Y'. Swedish 'obekväm' primarily means physically uncomfortable or inconvenient (obekväm stol, obekväm arbetstid); the mental-state sense governed by 'med att' is an anglicism, and stacking it under causative 'gör mig' compounds the strain — 'med'-phrase garden-paths as instrumental to 'gör'. Native alternative: 'Det gör mig obekväm inför att kalla en förflyttning för en metod' or better 'Det gör mig tveksam till att kalla en förflyttning för en metod'. Not lethal: 'vara obekväm med' is a spreading anglicism that does appear in edited contemporary Swedish debate prose.

findings.quote: lägger förstås märke till bristen tydligare än andra
findings.note: class 6: 'lägga märke till' is a punctual perception idiom that does not take a degree comparative like 'tydligare'; native alternative: 'märker bristen tydligare än andra' or 'lägger lättare märke till bristen'

findings.quote: Det gör mig obekväm med att kalla en förflyttning för en metod.
findings.note: class 2/5: causative 'göra mig obekväm med att' + infinitive mirrors English 'it makes me uncomfortable calling X a Y'; the anglicism 'obekväm med' lurches out of the otherwise traditional sakprosa register held by the rest of the essay; native alternative: 'Men jag har svårt att kalla en förflyttning för en metod.'

findings.quote: Nearly all of it is shielded now, and the town's total installed output has come down.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick C): A is eliminable from form alone as a double absolute ('every light in the valley', 'nothing ... any light upward') that no real code achieves, and C is then the only moderately hedged option ('Nearly all') among three sweeping claims (B 'has never established', D 'enough of them declined'). The hedging asymmetry pulls to C materially above chance, but B and D remain substantive alternative outcomes a passage would decide. Not a form-alone leak.

findings.quote: Nearly all their light fell inside one narrow band, which the observatory could screen out at little cost.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick B): low-pressure sodium emitting essentially at one narrow line, and observatories filtering that line cheaply, is standard astronomy knowledge, so a domain-aware solver picks B without the passage. But A (efficiency as the replacement motive), C (total light comparison) and D (filter cost in the blue) are all substantive, writable positions with no formal tell separating them; the mechanism is domain expertise, not structure. Routed to adjudication per calibration.

findings.quote: That it is too small to be told apart from other things that moved over the same years.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick D): C is eliminable from form as an over-general absolute ('cannot establish whether a lighting code has worked anywhere'), and A is a single-cause attribution to one event. The stem itself supplies the magnitude ('about three percent'), which primes the measurement-noise reading in D. B stays substantive, so the item is not decided blind, but two eliminations plus the stem's own small-number framing put a solver well above chance.

findings.quote: That a greenhouse kept lit all winter is the one thing now standing between the ridge and a usable sky.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick C): B is eliminable from form as a singleton absolute ('the one thing'), and A and D rest on the same underlying claim that light over the valley rose through the decade, which weakens both as a main-idea key. C is then the only option framing a metric-versus-reality mismatch, the shape main-idea keys usually take. A and D are separable claims a passage could distinguish, so this is an asymmetry lean rather than a form-alone leak.

findings.quote: That a name is chosen because no buyer is in a position to prove it inaccurate.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick B): a 3-1 asymmetry is visible without any domain knowledge - A (tested on customers), C (describes the shade closely enough) and D (defended against trade standards) all make the name answerable to something external, while B alone says the name is chosen precisely because it is unfalsifiable. The odd-one-out plus C reading as a bland truism pushes a solver above chance. It is not a form-alone leak: A and D are ordinary commercial practices a passage could equally well have keyed, so the pull is partly genre expectation that a short feature reports a surprising rule.

findings.quote: That the arrangement of the dimples has no bearing on the way a ball flies.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick C): D is eliminable from form as an absolute denial that is also plainly false in the world, and A's monotonic 'deeper dimples give longer flight' is contradicted by ordinary aerodynamics knowledge. The stem's framing ('implied', 'that ball makers advertise') primes a debunking key, which C supplies as the only hedged option ('can be smaller than'). B remains a substantive alternative, so the item is not decided blind; the mechanism is a mix of one formal absolute and golf-aerodynamics world knowledge.

findings.quote: Ekonomihistorikern Gunborg Sandell riktar en invandning ... mot Rahmqvists forklaring
findings.note: PARTIALLY: the stem asks for an objection to the EXPLANATION, and only D offers a rival explanation (wealth as confound); A (catalogue criteria widened 1958) and C (survivorship of the ornate towers) are objections to the DATA, a category mismatch a domain-free reader can see. The discipline label 'ekonomihistorikern' further narrows to the two economically framed options (B, D). Blind lean: D. Not a form-alone decision (B remains a substantive economic objection and the B-vs-D choice needs the passage), so flag, not kill.

findings.quote: Uppgiften var densamma i alla sjutton tornen, medan formen skiftade av skal som materialet bara delvis reder ut.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: on a generic 'vilket pastaende overensstammer bast' stem, B is the only non-committal umbrella claim; C overreaches ('samtliga ... bostader eller utsiktsplatser') and A overreaches in its second clause ('det var dessa som avgjorde utformningen'). Two overreach eliminations plus the measured-summary heuristic give a real edge over chance without the passage. Held at flag, not kill: D is also hedged ('tycks framfor allt'), so B is not the sole qualified option, and this is the standard shape of authentic HP global items, which the gate calibration says must not be killed.

findings.quote: Att utgiften inte upphör utan landar hos besökarna i stället för hos kommunen.
findings.note: B is an extreme proposal rather than an objection ('bemannade toaletter i varje kvarter i innerstaden, öppna dygnet runt') and C answers a different question than the stem asks (it explains the cause of the closures instead of objecting to them). The remaining pair is settled by the essay-thesis shape of A, so materially better than chance blind.

findings.quote: Matematikläxan var den läxa som oftast lämnades ogjord av eleverna.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick: none): D is eliminable from form as non-responsive - the stem asks what the time measurements showed, D reports completion rates - and C, the null result, is weakened by the presence of an exact mirror pair (A and B), which signals the author cared about the direction. That narrows the field to two, materially better than chance, but A and B are exact opposites and nothing in the stem or options decides between them, so the passage remains necessary.

findings.quote: Det största problemet i skolan är att lektionstiden inte räcker till för kursinnehållet.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick D): C falls from form as an off-topic superlative ('det största problemet i skolan') that answers a question the stem did not ask, and B is a policy prescription rather than a statement the text could be said to match. A overreaches by turning a study of homework time into a claim about what pupils learn. D is then the measured thesis that fits the study design. B is a real position in the Swedish debate rather than a caricature, so three eliminations of unequal strength - a lean, not a form-alone leak.
